questions.q: According to this lesson, is an enterprise structure built via rapid implementation spreadsheets exempt from testing and review?
options: No — whether built screen by screen or via RI spreadsheets, the structure should never go live untested
Only legal entities need review afterward
Only cross-validation rules need review afterward
Yes, RI-generated structures never need review
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states that an enterprise structure should never go live untested, regardless of how it was built.

questions.q: What does it mean to properly test a cross-validation rule?
options: Only confirming that valid combinations are accepted
Deliberately attempting both a known-bad combination (confirming rejection) and a known-good combination (confirming acceptance)
Deleting the rule and seeing if anyone notices
Running the rule only once during initial setup
questions.explain: A properly tested rule is checked on both sides: that it blocks the bad combinations it was designed to catch, and still allows the good ones through.

questions.q: Why is testing only the 'lets good combinations through' side of a cross-validation rule, while skipping the 'blocks bad ones' side, described as a costly shortcut?
options: Because this only matters for secondary ledgers
Because it has no real downside
Because a rule configured backward or scoped wrong will not announce the mistake itself, leaving bad combinations silently allowed
Because Oracle Fusion automatically detects backward rules
questions.explain: A rule that is misconfigured in a way that fails to block bad combinations won't reveal that mistake unless someone deliberately tests the blocking behavior.

questions.q: How should a consultant verify a hierarchy-based rollup report before trusting it?
options: By disabling the hierarchy entirely
By checking only the currency conversion rate used
By assuming it is correct since the hierarchy was built carefully
By pulling a report for a known parent node and manually verifying the total matches the sum of its expected children
questions.explain: Manually verifying a known parent's total against its expected children catches misattached or missing children before the error reaches real financial reporting.

questions.q: Why does this lesson emphasize reviewing the enterprise structure before go-live rather than after?
options: Because review after go-live is actually preferred
Because every item on the checklist is dramatically cheaper to fix before live transactions have posted against the structure
Because Oracle Fusion disables review after go-live
Because go-live automatically fixes any configuration errors
questions.explain: Catching configuration problems before transactions post is far less disruptive than correcting them afterward, a theme repeated throughout this course.
